pl-l3d27c4-d1e115.summary: Asks why, if the charity of God and of neighbor is one, it is called twofold.

pl-l3d27c4-d1e118.summary: Answers that it is because of two things loved, God and neighbor (man or angel); and so there are two commandments, since the same charity is commended in each, but different things are commanded to be loved.
claims: Charity is twofold by its objects.
The two commandments correspond to the two objects of love.

pl-l3d27c4-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: the Spirit was perhaps given twice, on earth and from heaven, to commend the two precepts of charity. One charity and two precepts, one Spirit and two givings, since only the charity that loves God loves the neighbor. They are perhaps called two because God and neighbor differ, one greater and one lesser, or because of two movements of the mind, moved much more toward God than toward neighbor.
claims: The charity that loves the neighbor is the same that loves God.
The mind is moved much more toward God than toward neighbor.

pl-l3d27c4.summary: Asks why charity is called twofold if it is one. Because of its two objects, God and neighbor (man or angel): one charity, two things loved, hence two commandments. Augustine connects this with the Spirit's being given twice, on earth and from heaven: one charity and two precepts, one Spirit and two givings, perhaps called two because God and neighbor differ, or because of two movements of the mind, toward God much more than toward neighbor.
claims: Charity is called twofold because of its two objects, not because there are two charities.
There are two commandments because different things are commanded to be loved.
The mind moves to love God much more than neighbor.
